meta.title: Local Flavors — Whizzzest
meta.description: A guide to the Six Bowls of Wanzai, Luocheng rice noodles, edible lily bulbs, sour jujube cake and traditional bamboo paper.

hero.title: Local flavors
hero.subtitle: Taste the signature dishes of Wanzai

dishes.title: Fugui Youjuan (Eight-Treasure Pork Rolls)
paras: The Six Bowls traditionally open with these sliced pork rolls. Pork, dried bamboo shoots and water chestnuts are among the ingredients wrapped in caul fat. The name Fugui evokes prosperity, making the rolls a fitting first dish at a banquet.

dishes.title: Wanzai Zharou (Steamed Pork Belly)
paras: This Wanzai banquet dish is made with pork belly that is seasoned, fried and steamed until tender. The slices have a glossy glaze and a rich, savory flavor.

dishes.title: Steamed Rice Flour with Pork
paras: This dish is also called Zharou in Wanzai, though its Chinese name is written differently from the pork belly dish. Rice flour supplies most of the body, while a smaller amount of pork gives it a savory flavor. Steaming makes the mixture soft and springy.

dishes.title: Wanzai Kuaiyu (Grass Carp Pieces)
paras: Pieces of grass carp are seasoned with rice wine lees and salt, fried until golden and then steamed. The wine lees lend the fish a mellow aroma. The dish is served at celebrations, where fish is associated with abundance.

dishes.title: Kangle Three-Yellow Chicken
paras: Kangle’s Three-Yellow Chicken takes its name from the bird’s yellow feathers, feet and beak. The chicken is gently simmered, producing clear broth and firm, tender meat. It is one of the Six Bowls.

dishes.title: Black Goat Soup
paras: Local black goat is simmered slowly to make a clear broth with tender pieces of meat. Wanzai families traditionally serve it around the winter solstice.

dishes.title: Luocheng Rice Noodles (Zhafen)
paras: Zhafen are Luocheng’s thick, pressed rice noodles. Made from early-season rice and dried in the sun, they stay firm when cooked. They are often stir-fried with soy seasoning and fresh chilies.

dishes.title: Wanzai Duorou (Chopped Pork with Chilies)
paras: Chopped pork is stir-fried with fresh chilies and garlic shoots. This spicy home-style dish is often served with a bowl of rice.

dishes.title: Wanzai Muscovy Duck
paras: In Wanzai, Muscovy duck is braised, simmered in clear broth or cooked with young ginger. A braised version with local ginger and garlic shoots is often served to guests.

dishes.title: Wanzai Lily Bulbs
paras: Longya, meaning “dragon’s tooth,” is a lily grown in Wanzai for its edible bulbs. The pale, mildly sweet bulbs are stir-fried, steamed or added to soups.

dishes.title: Biaoxin Paper
paras: Biaoxin paper is a traditional Wanzai specialty made from local moso bamboo. Its pale yellow sheets have fine, long fibers. The paper has been used in local rituals and folk customs.

dishes.title: Wanzai Sour Jujube Cake
paras: Made from sour jujubes, this amber, chewy fruit sweet has a tart finish. Wanzai Sour Jujube Cake is recognized as a geographical-indication product.

cta.title: Taste and take home
cta.desc: Find an itinerary with time for a local meal and a stop to shop for specialties.
